title: What If America Had Nuked the Moon?

scenes.text: What if America had nuked the Moon? In 1958, the Air Force seriously planned it.
The goal was a flash people on Earth could see, a morale boost after the Soviets took an early lead in the space race.
The warhead was a W25, about 1.7 kilotons, much smaller than the bomb that hit Hiroshima.
It would burst in the Moon's shadow, so sunlight lit the dust cloud. A young Carl Sagan calculated how that cloud would spread.
The Air Force canceled it in January 1959. The risks outweighed the benefits, including fallout that could spoil future lunar science.
The world only learned of it in 2000, when its leader, Leonard Reiffel, wrote to the journal Nature.

description:
What if America had nuked the Moon?
Project A119 was a real 1958 plan to explode a small nuclear warhead on the Moon so the flash could be seen from Earth. It was canceled in 1959.
